I think there are only a few reasonable paths:

1. A new content attribute name, which has reflection support. E.g. `<template shadowrootmode="">` with a reflecting (string-valued) `shadowRootMode` IDL attribute.

2. Keep the content attribute name, but remove the confusingly-overriden IDL attribute. In this world, we're making the decision that "parser macro" content attributes don't get reflection support.

3. A new content attribute name, but no reflection support. E.g. `<template shadowrootmode="">` with no reflecting IDL attribute.

The path of keeping the content attribute name, and making `HTMLTemplateElement.prototype.shadowRoot` reflect it, seems bad, because then `shadowRoot` means something different on `HTMLTemplateElement` than on every other element.

The current spec proposal, which introduces an IDL attribute with the same name as the content attribute, but that IDL attribute *isn't* providing reflection, is also very bad. Same-named IDL attributes need to do reflection.

```js
const container = document.createElement('div');
container.innerHTML = `<template shadowroot="open">x</template>`;

```

Sorry you're puzzled. The "initial PR" was 3.5 years ago, and a lot has happened in the intervening years. I've [shipped](https://chromestatus.com/feature/5191745052606464) and then [deprecated](https://chromestatus.com/feature/6239658726391808) the original `shadowroot` attribute in Chromium. As discussion resumed on the PR in 2023, we renamed to `shadowrootmode` and added the corresponding IDL. I had to push through some (reasonable) [opposition to bikeshedding after shipping](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/1n0MLr8G5NQ/m/TP3dAC8EAQAJ). I then [shipped again](https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161240576393216), with `shadowrootmode`, so that developers had something to migrate to from the old `shadowroot`. Five weeks ago, you requested the change from `DOMString?` to `DOMString` for `shadowRootMode` and I agreed, to try to finally get this PR landed. You then asked (just [above](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/5465#discussion_r1360613963)) whether this was "worth the churn". In general, through all of this, I'd say "no it has never been worth the churn". But I'd like to get this feature shipped interoperably, so as with the other changes, I went along with this one, and I'm ok keeping it as `DOMString`. Hopefully it's the last change, and we can finally land this PR.
